subject: Cooking
title: Specialty Coffee Scoring: The 100-Point Scale
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Specialty Coffee Scoring: The 100-Point Scale.

hook.text: Coffee is scored like wine — on a 100-point scale. Anything above 80 is 'specialty.' Above 90 is exceptional.

buildup.text: The Specialty Coffee Association (SCA) uses trained Q Graders who evaluate aroma, flavor, acidity, and body.

discovery.text: Q Graders undergo rigorous certification — including blind identification of 36 aromas and triangulation tests.

twist.text: Only 3% of the world's coffee scores above 85 points. The rest is commercial-grade — blended and sold cheaply.

climax.text: A 90+ score can increase a farmer's income tenfold — quality scoring is the path out of commodity pricing.

punchline.text: A number between 80 and 100 can change a farmer's entire life.

quiz.question: What score must coffee receive to be classified as 'specialty'?

details.summary: The Specialty Coffee Association rates coffee on a 100-point cupping scale evaluating aroma, flavor, aftertaste, acidity, body, balance, uniformity, clean cup, sweetness, and defects. Coffee scoring 80 or above is classified as specialty.
details.whyItMatters: The 100-point scale gave coffee a shared quality language, similar to wine ratings. It enabled consumers to differentiate quality and helped farmers earn premiums for exceptional beans.
takeaways: Coffee scoring 80 or above qualifies as specialty grade
Ten attributes are scored including aroma, acidity, body, and balance
The system created a quality hierarchy rewarding better farming practices

faq.question: What does a coffee cupping score actually measure?
faq.answer: Trained Q-graders evaluate ten attributes on a standardized scale: aroma, flavor, aftertaste, acidity, body, balance, uniformity, clean cup, sweetness, and overall impression. Defects are subtracted. Scores above 80 are specialty. Above 85 is excellent. Above 90 is exceptional and rare.

faq.question: How does the scoring system help coffee farmers?
faq.answer: Higher scores command higher prices on the specialty market. A 90-plus-point coffee may sell for five to ten times commodity price. This incentivizes farmers to invest in better processing, variety selection, and sustainable practices.
